evidence: Judged "What boundaries do I need to set as a result? What shaped the other person(s) into someone capable of that harm? What’s theirs and what’s mine?" inside the closing list of the section "Forgiveness without bypass", which the line above introduces as "Some questions that may be helpful to ask when coming to a place of forgiveness", against SOURCE (the approved working-copy questions "What boundaries need to be set? ... What is theirs? What is mine?", from his published four). The change does what the_change says: Emulate's rewording of the first question, his middle question word for word, and Emulate's merge of the last two into one. Meaning kept: which boundaries are needed, what shaped the other person into someone capable of that harm, and what is theirs and what is mine. The differences are small and add no fact: "do I need to set" puts the first question in the asker's own voice, which this list already uses ("What is mine" before it, "How can I let this go" after); "as a result" ties the boundaries to the impact asked just before, in line with the section's own "our boundary with them still matters"; the published "still needed" has no "still" in the draft, but the approved working copy it replaces has none either. It reads naturally in the list: each question follows the one before it, "as a result" points back at the answers to "What actually happened?" and "What was the impact?", "theirs" points at the other person(s) of the question just before it and "mine" at the asker (C02 absent), the middle question is untouched, and both "What’s" use the typographic apostrophe the rest of the section uses (don’t, we’re, aren’t), so there is no stray mark. Tell rows, T01-T29 and C01-C04, on the literal words in context: the one row actually happening is T02 at paragraph scale, seven short questions in a row, each doing one job and handing off (what happened, impact, boundaries, what shaped them, theirs and mine, accountability, letting go). I judge it justified: the run is the guide's own list (eight questions before this change, by my count of the source words plus the neighbours), the line above sets it up as a list of questions to ask, the text does not answer them itself, and the change shortens the run by merging two rather than adding any. T12: "theirs and mine" is a matched pair, but sorting whose is whose is the question's whole point and the source already had it as two questions, so it is a necessary contrast, not a pair made for balance. T11: "as a result" is the only connective and does real work in the list. T21: the merged question has a single job. T01 and C03: the "I" is the reader's own self-question, as in the last question, not the author's stake or a fact about Joel. T26: "set" and "boundaries" echo the section's earlier "set boundaries" as a callback, not an idle repeat. T19, T20 and T29: it sits mid-list and two more questions follow. T03-T10, T13-T18, T22-T25, T27, T28, C01 and C04: absent. Linter findings, each judged against the context: "B7 short landing at paragraph end" is accepted, because the linter saw the draft alone; in the article "What’s theirs and what’s mine?" is followed by "What does accountability require?" and the last question, and the paragraph lands on the unchanged "How can I let this go, without denying any of the above?". "D9 follows the source order" is accepted: it keeps the source's order and reorders nothing, and the passage still notices things through its unchanged parts (the last question calls back "the above"). The O29 run of three questions is accepted: they are the reflection prompts the line above introduces, not questions the text answers itself, a reader would ask each of them, and the run is his published list, which the change leaves no longer.
